label: Fixed-term employment: period beyond which the contract is treated as open-ended
appliesTo: Fixed-term employees, including foreign nationals on work statuses
why: Usually stated as an automatic conversion, and the exceptions are what make it wrong for exactly the population this site writes for — foreign professionals are frequently engaged under the professional knowledge and skills exception, so the two-year clock does not work the way a general article implies.

history.source: Act on the Protection of Fixed-Term and Part-Time Employees
history.note: As a rule a fixed-term employee may not be used beyond two years, and continuous employment past it is treated as a contract without a fixed term. Statutory exceptions allow longer engagement — completion of a defined project, covering an absent employee, education and training periods, older workers, and the use of professional knowledge or skills among them. The last of those covers a great deal of foreign professional hiring, so 'two years means automatic permanence' is not a safe reading.
